title: Minor-key harmony
description: Drill natural-minor RN, harmonic V/V7, and v vs V7 cadences on guitar.

cards.front: Why is minor-key harmony not one fixed scale?
cards.back: Natural minor supplies the diatonic set; harmonic minor (raised 7) creates major V / V7 and a leading tone; melodic minor (raised 6 and 7) appears in lines and some chord colors.

cards.front: List the natural-minor diatonic triads of A minor with Roman numerals.
cards.back: i Am, ii° B°, ♭III C, iv Dm, v Em, ♭VI F, ♭VII G.

cards.front: In A minor, what does raising G to G♯ change on degrees 5 and 7?
cards.back: v becomes V (E) or V7 (E7). vii° becomes sharper leading-tone material (G♯°).

cards.front: Why does E7 → Am feel conclusive?
cards.back: E7 comes from harmonic minor. Its G♯ is the leading tone and pulls to A.

cards.front: Why does natural minor’s ♭7 make v a weak pull to i?
cards.back: ♭7 keeps the chord on 5 minor (Em in A minor). There is no leading tone into the tonic.

cards.front: What harmonic color can raised 6 (melodic minor) add in minor?
cards.back: It smooths motion into the leading tone and can yield major IV color.

cards.front: What must Roman numerals in minor make clear about degree 5?
cards.back: Whether you assume natural minor (v) or include harmonic-minor chords (V / V7).

cards.front: Name three common minor-key mixes of these resources.
cards.back: i–iv–V7–i; i–♭VII–♭VI–V; Aeolian rock loops with ♭VII. Classical minor uses raised leading tones.

cards.front: What does analysis ask first in a minor progression?
cards.back: Which 6 and 7 are in play — natural, raised, or mixed.

cards.front: In A minor, compare | Am | Dm | Em | Am | with | Am | Dm | E7 | Am |.
cards.back: The first keeps natural v. The second uses harmonic V7; hear G♯ pull to A.

cards.front: When voice-leading E7 into Am, which two notes resolve, and where?
cards.back: G♯ → A (leading tone up) and D → C (seventh down).

cards.front: What is a typical authentic verse Aeolian close in minor?
cards.back: Authentic is often V7 → i. Aeolian closes may use ♭VII → i, with different weight.

cards.front: Write the natural-minor diatonic triads of E minor with RN.
cards.back: i Em, ii° F♯°, ♭III G, iv Am, v Bm, ♭VI C, ♭VII D.

cards.front: Write the natural-minor diatonic triads of D minor with RN.
cards.back: i Dm, ii° E°, ♭III F, iv Gm, v Am, ♭VI B♭, ♭VII C.

cards.front: Spell V7 of A minor from harmonic minor. Show the leading tone resolving in note names.
cards.back: E7 is E G♯ B D. G♯ resolves to A.

cards.front: Analyze | Am | F | G | E7 | Am | with RN. Which chord needs raised 7?
cards.back: i – ♭VI – ♭VII – V7 – i. E7 needs raised 7 (G♯).

cards.front: A 4-bar minor phrase uses ♭VII and ends V7–i. In A minor, what chords is that?
cards.back: G is ♭VII; the cadence is E7 → Am. Example shape: start on Am, pass through G, end E7–Am.
